description: At the Urban Planet Lab, we study how growing cities and a changing climate interact as two dynamically interacting complex systems. Extreme heat is an emergent phenomenon resulting from this interaction and is our flagship problem. But our approach extends to the broader ways urbanization reshapes climate, ecosystems, and human wellbeing. We combine complexity science, urban climate modeling, and remote sensing to understand how climate extremes impact cities and the citizens, who bears the worst burden, and how we can build a more resilient urban future for all.
hero_image_alt: Research at The Urban Planet Lab
section_description: Our work spans four interconnected areas, each addressing critical dimensions of sustainable urban futures.
closing_statement: Through rigorous science and society partnerships, we aim to produce knowledge that is not only academically rigorous but practically actionable for cities worldwide.
